title: GraphMind: Unveiling Scientific Reasoning through Contextual Graphs for Novelty Assessment

problem.claim: Scientific novelty assessment requires evaluating both a paper's internal structure and its contribution within the broader research landscape.

gap.claim: Existing LLM approaches often rely on surface-level similarity or citation retrieval and overlook the integration of paper content with contextual grounding in related literature.

contributions.claim: SciNova is a benchmark containing 3,063 ICLR and NeurIPS papers with full content, bibliographies, and peer review scores for novelty prediction.
GraphMind jointly processes micro- and macro-level structures for novelty prediction and rationale generation.
GraphMind represents papers and related works as hierarchical graphs capturing claims, methods, experiments, cited works, and semantically similar works.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly introduce the SciNova benchmark and propose GraphMind as a bi-level graph model for novelty prediction and rationale generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that incorporating the bi-level graph significantly outperforms baseline LLMs in novelty score prediction and rationale generation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Scientific novelty assessment must account for both internal paper structure and broader research context.
Existing LLM approaches inadequately integrate paper content with contextual grounding in related literature.
The authors introduce SciNova as a benchmark for novelty prediction.
The authors propose GraphMind, which jointly models micro- and macro-level graph structures.
The authors report improved novelty prediction and rationale generation over baseline LLMs.

source_observation.claim: The proposed model jointly represents a paper's internal components and its relationships to cited and semantically similar works.

interpretation.claim: Novelty assessment may benefit from combining document-internal structure with contextual literature structure.

application.claim: For comparable assessment tasks, model both the target artifact's internal evidence and its external relational context.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported novelty prediction setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset splits, evaluation metrics, baseline details, or numerical performance results.
The abstract does not describe the rationale-generation evaluation protocol or the quality of peer review scores.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported improvements.
